newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nordic bank sets Aug 15 for Taiwan-dlr bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Nordic bank sets Aug 15 for Taiwan-dlr bond issue.

text.p: The Nordic Investment Bank (NIB) has scheduled its T$4 billion (US$143 million) Taiwan dollar-denominated bond issue for August 15, lead underwriter Citicorp International Securities said on Friday.
The bond would mature on August 15, 2002, Citicorp said.
"The coupon rate, which was also determined today (Friday), is 6.08 percent," said Albert Wang, head of Citicorp's fixed income division.
Citicorp said the Nordic bank decided to make the issue because Taiwan's interest rates have hovered at high levels.
"This is one of the advantages of this bond which makes it an attractive investment," Citicorp said on Wednesday when it disclosed the issue.

Taiwan's overnight interbank rate soared above double digits in late June before easing in early July. It was trading at 7.427 percent on Friday, still well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Nordic Investment Bank would become the fourth international bank to issue Taiwan-dollar bonds.
The latest international bank to issue Taiwan-dollar bonds was the Central American Bank of Economic Integration, which made a T$6.8 billion issue on May 16.
The other two banks that have launched issues were the Asian Development Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
On Thursday Taiwan's central bank said both the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank also have expressed interest in launching issues.
